NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An elder remembers the old war chant from the last raid, long ago: teach it to the warriors, or let it rest.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When (subject) was a child, raiders came, and the village drove them off with a chant that made the ground tremble. (subject) is one of the few left who remembers it. (friend) has asked (subject.him/her) to teach it to the warriors now. (subject) has not sung it in sixty years, and does not want to remember why. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) teaches it, line by line, very quietly. Then the warriors sing it together, loud, and (subject) has to sit down. Afterwards, (subject.he/she) tells (friend), just once, about the night the raiders came. Then (subject.he/she) asks never to talk about it again. (friend) promises.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) says the old chant belongs to the old night, and asks (friend) to make a new one. (friend) does, with the warriors. It is rougher and louder and full of things about fish. (subject) listens from the edge of the beach, and nods.
